name: light fire
_note: without matches or 2 stones: friction with 2 dry sticks (firewood), 1 h, catches 2 times in 3; the wood (3 to burn, 2 sticks) is only used when it catches
log: You twist a dry stick against a branch, again and again, until your palms burn.
No matches. You spin a stick between your hands until your arms ache.
You rub wood on wood, slow and stubborn, blowing on every wisp of smoke.

text: A glow, a breath, and at last a flame. The fire takes.
The wisp of smoke becomes an ember, then a flame.
Finally, a flame. You feed it, careful as with a newborn.
Smoke, but no flame. The wood will do for another try.
The ember dies before it catches. You keep the wood.
At length fatigue compels you to stop; the sticks have yielded no fire.
